# Structure

Candidate definition: **structure** is the arrangement of elements and their relationships within a stated view and boundary. A **structural description** represents that arrangement; it may describe membership, interfaces, responsibility arrangements or information relationships. The description and the arrangement it describes are distinct.

Structure does not alone describe how things behave over time or demonstrate that they work. A topic bank containing topic pages describes an arrangement; the discovery, ordering and selection activity describes execution. The arrangement can be well documented while no useful execution has occurred.

Structural composition differs from dependency and contribution. A retained source can support a claim without being an operating component of the assessed system. Classification also differs: being a kind of something does not mean being its constituent part.

The [relationship vocabulary](../relationships.md) owns these distinctions; [mereology](../../mereology/composition-and-boundaries.md) owns composition rules. Exact process/structure/system boundaries remain EOM-10 in [the ledger](../../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a).
